userIntent: Continue natural development by mapping one immutable Gen0-8 Weak/Medium/Strong RGB swatch to four logical CERN quads A/B/C/D, each reporting a different view.

inputs.sourceRegistry: Wakaku virtual 370 hue addresses, mode=hue, 3 fixed orbits

quadViews.label: ALICE
quadViews.validation: Hue recomputed from frozen generation/index; original hue must match

quadViews.label: ATLAS
quadViews.validation: RGB hex recomputed from hue and intensity by additive HSV conversion; no detector data

quadViews.label: CMS
quadViews.validation: Selected amplitude and peer strengths agree with generation and index

quadViews.label: LHCb
quadViews.validation: Nearest fixed Wakaku hue address and orbit independently recomputed

quorum.rule: At least 3 distinct named quad reports must declare the same identity key and pass their own local consistency checks.
quorum.simulation: Inject 0,1,2 or 4 altered software reports without modifying the canonical swatch.
quorum.oneBad: 3/4 reports can still agree and accept, while showing disagreement.
quorum.fourCoherentlyBad: Shared coordinated corruption can still agree, illustrating lack of independent physical sources.
quorum.scope: Quorum of derived software representations is not a cryptographic signature, independent detector witness, proof of source truth or new particle evidence.

limitations: Every software quad inspects the same generated color swatch. Their projections are algorithmically distinct but NOT statistically independent measurements.
Quad labels reference ALICE, ATLAS, CMS, LHCb by logical mnemonic only; no CERN experiment provided optical color data, and only ATLAS has three toroidal detector magnets.
Strength W/M/S corresponds to 1/3,2/3,1 HSV value; NOT electroweak, intermediate, or strong nuclear interaction strength.
The 370 existing source color addresses and all earlier frozen module artifacts are read-only.
Agreement among mutually derived projections does not establish physical truth; coordinated fake reports can pass quorum.
